dataset.name: Groundwater and surface water head from 2019 to 2022 at the Tims Branch in Savannah River Site (SRS), South Carolina.
description: This dataset contains groundwater and surface water head measurements for investigating hydro-biogeochemical processes in Tims Branch at the Savannah River Site, SC. Water levels were monitored using pressure transducers installed in surface water gauges and piezometers across three subsites in Tims Branch, identified as Wfloc, Snon (Snon1 and Snon2), and Sfloc. A barometric pressure logger was deployed in piezometers to correct pressure transducers from atmospheric pressure. Manual water level measurements were taken to calibrate transducer data. The dataset consists of at least paired groundwater and surface water head time series for each subsite, provided as individual CSV files. These data support analyses of surface-groundwater interactions, hydrologic controls on redox processes, and broader synthesis of wetland hydrology at the Savannah River Site.

spatialCoverage.description: Tims Branch is a third-order stream located within the U.S. Department of Energy’s Savannah River Site (SRS) in Aiken County, South Carolina, USA. The study site is a low-relief, densely vegetated riparian wetland hydraulically connected to the main Tims Branch channel, approximately 3 km upstream of a known uranium-contaminated reach. This wetland and adjacent channel sections naturally contain elevated iron and organic carbon and are characterized by the presence of iron flocs that vary spatially and temporally with hydrologic conditions and can immobilize metals such as uranium.

measurementTechnique: At each subsite, a piezometer and a surface water gauge were hand-installed to quantify vertical water movement. Piezometers consisted of ~1.83 m of solid PVC pipe connected to a ~30 cm screened interval to measure shallow groundwater head. Surface water gauges were fully screened and installed to a depth sufficient to remain upright while measuring surface water levels. Levelogger pressure transducers were deployed in all piezometers and surface water gauges to record water levels at 15-minute intervals. A barometric pressure logger was installed in one piezometer to correct pressure transducer measurements for atmospheric pressure. In addition, a pressure transducer and conductivity probe were installed at subsites SNon2 (flocs absent) and WFloc (microbial mats present). Manual water-level measurements were collected at known times for all piezometers and surface water gauges to calibrate pressure records and calculate hydraulic heads for porewater and surface water.

Pressure transducer data were downloaded from the Leveloggers and corrected for atmospheric pressure using barometric measurements in Levelogger software. Manual water-level measurements from each surface water gauge and piezometer were used to calibrate hydraulic heads derived from the compensated water-level records.
